reasons.A: Understands form intake and free software; no security/performance guarantees. Explicitly distinguishes a proposed setup price from existing product pricing.
reasons.B: Agency owners have authority, repeated intake and a kickoff trigger. Solo brand designers substantially overlap in workflow and buying process. Evidence of urgency is rightly requested rather than assumed.
reasons.C: Chooses a sales-assisted paid setup service instead of explaining Tally's self-service software monetisation. Templates are a relevant alternative, but the plan tests a different offer/business model. Authorization caveat is honest and necessary, yet unresolved.
reasons.D: Public directories and permitted business routes are concrete. Eight researched, qualified, personalised invitations in 24 minutes are not credible; the paid pilot scope and several important notes are unfinished. Decision branches test urgency/approval and stop if the free workaround suffices.
reasons.E: Separates activation and payment and admits paid-plan uncertainty. The €49 price is explicitly a test, not a claimed Tally tariff, but has no delivery economics or defined finished scope. No arbitrary response-rate benchmark.
reasons.F: Several fields end abruptly, including first-buyer rationale, payment scope and commercial learning. Time allocation is unrealistic. Messages are usable questions and avoid fabricated observations; the overall contract remains incomplete.

excerpts: The supplied product claims describe free forms, not a verified paid plan.
If authorized, test a clearly scoped €49 pilot: configure
Research and qualify eight agency owners, sending one personalized invitation wherever an appropriate public contact route exists.
criticalBlockers: Unachievable research/outreach scope within numeric time allowance
Proposed service revenue is not a demonstrated path to paying SaaS customers
